content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment values) — reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is rising.
- Underestimate prices during strong negative sentiment — increase forecast lows when sentiment is bearish.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast increases after a +0.30+ sentiment spike to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean-revert forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — if sentiment < -0.30 for 3+ days, reduce forecast slope toward prior 10-day average.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast is high 3–5 days after a price spike, reduce by 5–10% to account for delayed market correction.
- Avoid forecasting upward trends when sentiment is flat or mildly negative — if sentiment < -0.20 for 2+ consecutive days, cap forecast growth at prior 7-day average.
